{{Quote|There's nothing like facing down a ghest in the swamps of Rodia and knowing you only have one shot to put it down. Now that's fun!|The big-game hunter War'qi, claiming to have fought a ghest|<ref name="GFT:PG">''[[Gundark's Fantastic Technology: Personal Gear]]''</ref>}}
'''Ghests''', also known as '''swamp demons''', were a large [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]]. Instead of [[Bone/Legends|bone]], the species had cartilaginous skeletons. The [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Rodian/Legends|Rodians]], who feared the predators because they sometimes attacked entire primitive Rodian [[City/Legends|villages]], originally believed ghests to be responsible for carrying away the [[Soul/Legends|souls]] of the [[Death/Legends|dead]]. Ghests hunted by swimming slowly along the surface of the [[Water/Legends|water]] and lashing out at their prey, usually large [[Diet/Legends|herbivores]], often swallowing them in one bite. When [[Reproduction/Legends|mating]], ghests performed a courtship ritual that proved their strength to the partner. A ghest [[Parent/Legends|mother]] guarded her [[Youngling/Legends|young]] after reproduction, as the sire would simply eat them on sight.

As Rodian culture developed, the ghest population diminished both as a result of [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]], particularly by those Rodians known as [[ghestslayer]]s, and the industrialization of Rodia's environment. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] made contact with Rodia, the predators were nearly extinct. In an attempt to save the species, some wealthy Rodians attempted to introduce ghest populations onto other worlds. A ghest attacked the crew of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[FarStar]]'' on the planet [[Danoor]] in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Ghest-CoG.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Ghests possessed razor-sharp teeth.]]
Ghests were a [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of predatory [[Reptile/Legends|reptile]] with cartilaginous [[Bone/Legends|skeletons]]. They possessed a pair of bulbous, featureless [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and a [[Mouth/Legends|maw]] full of razor-sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|338|ghest}}</ref> surrounded by a patch of bumpy, differently shaded skin.<ref name="TEGtPaM">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> Their head was located at the end of a long, slender body, which was, on average, six [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length.<ref name="CoG" /> They possessed slick skin,<ref name="KO">''[[The Kathol Outback]]''</ref> a tail, and four relatively thin [[Limb/Legends|limbs]]: two forelimbs and two larger hindlimbs, all ending in four thick, clawed digits. Where the forelimbs attached to the body beneath the head, the skin was particularly wrinkled.<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> The species had two [[Gender/Legends|genders]] and [[Reproduction/Legends|reproduced]] sexually; indeed, the females could even extract and use [[sperm]] from [[Death/Legends|dead]] male members of the species. Once fertilized, a female laid hundreds of [[Egg/Legends|eggs]]. These eggs developed into [[Youngling/Legends|juvenile]] ghests, which appeared as much smaller versions of their [[Parent/Legends|parents]]. Juveniles grew into a pre-adult stage before reaching full maturity.<ref name="CoG" />

==Behavior==
Ghests lived in the [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] and bayous of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]], where they usually hunted large species of [[Diet/Legends|herbivore]].<ref name="CoG" /> They could walk on their hind limbs while on land<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> but hunted and mated while submerged in [[Water/Legends|water]]. Ghests swam slowly when hunting, keeping all but their eyes and forehead submerged below the surface until they spotted prey. Upon seeing a target, a ghest sprang forward, attacked with teeth and claws, and generally consumed the prey in a single bite. However, it was not unknown for ghests to attack small [[City/Legends|settlements]] belonging to the sentient [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] species, also native to Rodia; during some such attacks, the ghest devoured all residents<ref name="CoG" /> within a few [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]].<ref name="SOTEP">''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]''</ref> The ghests had no natural predators on Rodia, although Rodians did sometimes [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] them.<ref name="CoG" />

When mating, ghests performed a courtship ritual that was a mixture of dance and combat. Both ghests involved tried to prove they were of equal strength to the other, as only individuals of matching prowess made suitable mates. Behavioral [[Zoologist/Legends|zoologists]] hypothesized that the fighting was at least partially due to each ghest's urge to stop other ghests from reproducing, which conflicted with their own desire to mate. Female ghests generally fought harder than males, and if a female killed her partner, she could still extract his sperm and reproduce. If a female died in a fight, though, no reproduction could take place. After mating, the pair split apart and moved away from each other at top speed due to a natural instinct to prevent the male from meeting and devouring his offspring. Alone, the female laid her eggs in a small pool and then protected them while they developed. Upon hatching, juvenile ghests fed on each other, ensuring only the strongest survived to the pre-adult stage. Those that lived then buried themselves in mud to hide from their mother, who would consume any juvenile ghests she saw outside the pool in the event that it was not one of her own offspring. Once all of the ghests in a pool were dead or hidden, the mother lost interest and departed. At that point, the pre-adults were free to emerge safely and leave.<ref name="CoG" />

==History==
During the early development of the Rodian species, ghests stood above the sentient Rodians in the [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] chain, as Rodians could not match the predators in size or ferocity.<ref name="SOTEP" /> Due to the danger ghests posed over the [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]]<ref name="SWRPG2ND">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> of the Rodians' early history, the predators came to hold an important place in Rodian myths and legends. Rodians sometimes knew ghests as swamp [[Demon/Legends|demons]], and ancient Rodians believed that ghests captured the [[Soul/Legends|spirits]] of the dead; thus, sightings of the species were considered bad omens. Killing a ghest was believed to remove a curse, such as a drought or famine, so groups of male Rodians sometimes banded together to ritually hunt down a ghest and kill it.<ref name="CoG" /> As Rodians could not physically compete with the beasts, they instead outsmarted them, eventually developing weapons and tools that could be used to stake out areas of jungle and defend them from ghests and other predators.<ref name="SOTEP" />

As Rodian culture developed, much of the folklore surrounding the ghest was diminished, but they were still often used as demons in [[Rodian Theater/Legends|Rodian Theater]],<ref name="CoG" /> with an entire genre named "Ghest" focusing on the ancient attacks on Rodian villages.<ref name="SOTEP" /> Hunting ghests became more common as Rodian civilization developed, and some Rodians came to work as [[ghestslayer]]s; the ghestslayer [[Kalon Lenitor]] was considered legendary.<ref name="air">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref> Due to such hunting and the industrialization of Rodia, ghests slowly became less common in their natural habitat as the Rodians became more advanced.<ref name="CoG" /> By the [[Time/Legends|time]] that [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] first discovered Rodia and introduced the Rodians to [[Realspace/Legends|space]] travel, the ghests were on the verge of [[extinction]].<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> To combat the decline of the ghest population on their homeworld, some wealthy Rodians attempted to introduce populations of juvenile ghests to other [[Planet/Legends|planets]], where they might survive.<ref name="CoG" /> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Rodian [[Entukan Yesosko]] was the leading [[Actor/Legends|actress]] in ghest plays.<ref name="SOTEP">''[[Shadows of the Empire Planets Guide]]''</ref>

==Ghests in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Herald, I bartered away small hunt trophies. Two ghest skins, rack of horax teeth.|Qyzen Fess|<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=conversation|Qyzen Fess|The Scorekeeper's Lesson}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ghest_attack.jpg|thumb|right|100px|A ghest attacks the crew of the ''FarStar'' on the planet Danoor.]]
The [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] hunter [[Qyzen Fess]], who lived during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], hunted several ghests during his career.<ref name="TOR" /> Over three thousand years later, by [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> at least one ghest had been transplanted to the planet [[Danoor]] in the [[Kathol Outback/Legends|Kathol Outback]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. The ghest lived in the murky rainwater that filled a series of [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] tunnels once used as an irrigation system for [[Farm/Legends|farmland]] but abandoned after the city of [[Eror Zeen]] was built on the fields. At one point, the creature attacked several crew members of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[FarStar]]'' while they were making their way through the tunnels with the [[Navigator/Legends|navigator]] [[Makezh]].<ref name="KO" /> Also during the New Republic's reign, the [[Big game hunter/Legends|big-game hunter]] [[War'qi]] claimed to have fought a ghest on Rodia using a [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech]] [[Firearc49 Speargun]], an experience he supposedly enjoyed. The claim was included as a note posted on an entry for the weapon in an [[Gundark's Gear Datalog|arms datalog]] created by the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Arms dealer/Legends|arms dealer]] known as [[Gundark (arms dealer)|Gundark]].<ref name="GFT:PG" />

==Behind the scenes==
Ghests were first mentioned in ''[[Creatures of the Galaxy]]'', a sourcebook released in [[1994]] for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. Ghests were first designed by [[Peter Venters]], who created the illustration shown in the book, which was then given to writer [[Chuck Truett]] so he could create the creature's backstory and rules based on the image.<ref name="CoG" /> Ghests also made an appearance in ''[[The Kathol Outback]]'' adventure ''[[Galaxy's Edge]]'', released in [[1996]], in which one was illustrated by [[Dan Day]] and [[David Day]]. In the adventure, a ghest attacks the players, although they are left with the decision of whether to kill it or simply escape from it, with no preferred method indicated.<ref name="KO" />
